jobs.title: Assistant GIS Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Randstad Digital is seeking a Assistant GIS Specialist for an exciting opportunity in Akron, OH. The Assistant Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Specialist supports the development, maintenance, analysis, and management of GIS data for a wide range of professional services. This role assists with GIS analysis, data development, data maintenance, and data preparation for use in GIS applications. A key responsibility of the position is providing excellent customer service by regularly communicating project status and collaborating with clients to ensure project objectives are met.

Working closely with cross-functional teams, the Assistant GIS Specialist delivers high-quality GIS data and services while demonstrating a strong commitment to teamwork, customer service, responsiveness, and continuous improvement.

location: Akron, Ohio

job type: Contract

salary: $25.00 - 27.72 per hour

work hours: 8am to 5pm

education: Bachelors

Responsibilities

Assist with GIS analysis, data development, data collection, and mapping for client projects while supporting both internal and external project teams.
Assist with GIS metadata creation, digital feature extraction, land survey record searches, and ownership data research from a variety of sources.
Assist with coordinate system projections and geospatial data transformations for project deliverables.
Assist in creating and updating GIS maps, map layers, and geospatial databases.
Assist with georeferencing raster and vector datasets.
Support ad-hoc analyses and provide recommendations to help achieve business goals related to quality, billability, and utilization.
Assist with quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) of GIS deliverables to ensure compliance with client and project requirements.
Utilize software applications and information from various sources (e.g., Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Excel, deeds, field notes, and other project documentation) to develop GIS maps supporting field personnel and client deliverables.
Regularly communicate project status with project teams and clients to support successful project execution.
Ensure compliance with company and site safety policies.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Geography, Geomatics, Computer Science, or a closely related field.

GIS Professional (GISP) certification or an ESRI technical certification is preferred but not required.

Ability to work independently while demonstrating accuracy, reliability, sound judgment, and problem-solving skills.

Ability to work methodically and analytically in a quantitative problem-solving environment with demonstrated critical thinking skills.

Basic proficiency with ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online (AGOL), and Microsoft Office applications.

Strong attention to detail with excellent organizational, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Demonstrated initiative and the ability to work effectively in a team environment.

Prior Internship And/or Related Consulting Experience Is Preferred.

Minimum GPA of 3.0 is strongly preferred.

A master's degree in a related field may be substituted for one year of experience.

jobs.title: Civil & Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
About The Role:

The Civil & Environmental Engineer plays a key role in supporting our clients mine closure, rehabilitation, and resource development activities through the design, planning, and delivery of practical water management and civil engineering solutions. Working closely with our Resource Development, Operations, and Environmental teams, you'll help ensure our sites achieve their operational, environmental, and long-term closure objectives.

The ideal candidate will be based in either Auckland or Hamilton, with the ability to commute the North Waikato mine site

This role is heavily focused on surface water management, drainage design, erosion and sediment control, landform development, and mine closure engineering. You'll contribute to a range of projects from concept development and modelling through to construction support and implementation, helping to deliver sustainable outcomes across our client's operations and future developments.

The ideal applicant will hold a Bachelor of Engineering (Civil or Environmental) and have experience in civil, water, environmental, or mining engineering. You'll bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, enjoy working across multidisciplinary teams, and be confident balancing technical requirements with practical operational needs. Experience with hydrological modelling, GIS, civil design software, and surface water infrastructure design will be highly regarded.

jobs.title: Managing Technical Consultant, Environmental Permitting / Due Diligence Project Manager
jobs.description:
Are you looking for a chance to lead, innovate, and create lasting environmental impact? Join ERM
and help us build a sustainable future in Seattle, WA
.

Why This Role Matters

Are you ready to lead transformative environmental strategies for some of the most innovative technology infrastructure projects in the world? At ERM, we’re not just managing compliance—we’re shaping the future of sustainable development. This is your opportunity to join a global leader and make a measurable impact on projects that define tomorrow’s technology landscape.

What Your Impact Is

As a Managing Technical Consultant, Environmental Permitting / Due Diligence Project Manager,
you’ll be at the forefront of ERM’s Capital Project Delivery (CPD) service line, driving environmental permitting and due diligence for major capital projects. Your leadership will ensure that technology sector infrastructure developments meet environmental standards while advancing sustainability goals. You’ll influence decisions at the highest level, collaborate with global experts, and deliver solutions that balance innovation with environmental stewardship.

What You’ll Bring

Required:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in engineering, environmental science, biology/ecology, planning, program management, or a related field. Or equivalent experience.
4+ years of relevant experience in environmental permitting and/or due diligence.
Proven ability to manage complex projects, meet deadlines, and lead multidisciplinary teams.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing technical reports and presenting to clients.
Ability to build and maintain client relationships and thrive in a fast-paced consulting environment.
This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Preferred:

Experience with permitting timelines, risk identification, and mitigation strategies.
Technical skills in wildlife or ecological surveys (e.g., wetland delineations, wildlife assessments).
Familiarity with air quality permitting and multi-media regulatory compliance programs.

Key Responsibilities

Lead environmental risk evaluations, permitting, and approvals for technology infrastructure and major capital projects.
Identify permitting requirements during site acquisition and due diligence processes.
Manage regulatory agency interactions and develop mitigation strategies for environmental risks.
Collaborate with architecture and engineering partners on conceptual master planning.
Communicate environmental requirements to diverse stakeholders, including legal, real estate, design, and sustainability teams.
Oversee preparation of reports, permitting documents, and environmental reviews at federal and state levels.
Serve as project manager, technical expert, and QA/QC reviewer to ensure quality and compliance.
Drive business development through proposal preparation and client relationship management.
Monitor project performance, budgets, schedules, and health & safety protocols.
Work across ERM’s global network to share best practices and deliver exceptional results.

For the Managing Technical Consultant, Environmental Permitting / Due Diligence Project Manager position, the anticipated annual base pay is $90,000 – $124,245 USD
. Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, parental leave, medical, dental, vision, life, disability, AD&D insurance, 401(k) or RRSP/DPSP, and other applicable benefits to eligible employees.

Note
: Bonuses, commissions, and other forms of additional compensation are not guaranteed and subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures.

Who We Are:

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!

jobs.title: Environmental Test Laboratory Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About The Role

As Validation Laboratory Module Lead
, you build Harmattan's environmental test laboratory from a blank page and then run it. Today too much of our environmental testing depends on external labs and their scheduling, which slows our development down as much as it costs us. Your mission is to change that, and you own it end to end: defining the capabilities we need, specifying and buying the machines, contributing to the choice of premises, recruiting and leading the technicians, and drawing the line between what we bring in-house and what stays external.

This is a senior, hands-on leadership role, and the lab does not exist yet. Beyond building it, you become the Group's reference on environmental testing: supporting the validation teams on the lab validation of their projects, reviewing the environmental parts of their test plans, and handing our test procedures over to the quality team as products move into production.

What You'll Do

Define the lab and select the equipment: Establish the capabilities we need, then specify, evaluate and procure the machines, covering climatic and thermal cycling, water and dust ingress, vibration and UV ageing, including a large climate room in which we can fly a drone under controlled wind and temperature.
Decide what we internalise and what stays external: Draw the line between the tests worth owning and those better bought from external labs, such as accredited qualification or rare capital-heavy tests, and revisit that line as our product range grows.
Set up the facility: Contribute to the choice of premises, then take the site from layout and utilities through to installation, safety and commissioning.
Build and lead the team: Recruit and lead a team of two to three lab technicians, set the working standards, and grow the team's capability as the lab ramps up.
Support the validation teams: Assist the validation modules on the lab validation of their projects, and peer-review the environmental sections of their test plans, making sure the right tests, conditions and acceptance criteria are defined.
Hand over to production: Work with the quality team to transfer our test procedures as products reach PVT and mass production, so that production-line testing stays consistent with what validation defined.

What We're Looking For

At least 10 years in environmental testing, including setting up or substantially developing a test lab. This is a senior role and we are looking for depth, not a first lab job.
Strong command of environmental test methods and the equipment behind them: climatic and thermal cycling, vibration, water and dust ingress, UV, and the standards that frame them.
Proven equipment judgement: able to specify, evaluate and procure test machines, and to argue build-versus-buy and in-house-versus-external on both cost and technical merit.
Experience leading a small technical team, or clear readiness to step into that responsibility.
A rigorous, methodical approach to test planning, acceptance criteria and documentation.
Comfortable working across functions with engineering, validation and quality, and translating between them.
Engineering degree in a relevant field (mechanical, materials, electronics, physics or similar), or equivalent experience.
Bonus: experience with defence or aerospace test standards (MIL-STD-810, RTCA DO-160 or similar); familiarity with lab accreditation and metrological traceability such as ISO/IEC 17025; a background in drones or robotics.
Working-level English; French is a plus.
Based at our Paris-area site, with occasional travel to our Swiss site.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.
